governanceNotes: D1 batch 63 (2026-09-26): five bounded association edges authored - nephrosis to deep-vein-thrombosis (rank 1), to pulmonary-embolism (rank 2), to cerebrovascular-accident-stroke-residuals (rank 3), to myocardial-infarction (rank 4), and to chronic-kidney-disease (rank 5) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The thromboembolic propositions rest on the Danish national matched cohort of 3,967 first-time nephrotic adults (PMID 34979093), the edema-stratified multicenter cohort of 1,219 nephrotic-range patients (PMID 40043694), the antithrombin hypercoagulability multi-cohort meta-analysis (PMID 36754010), and the cardiovascular risk review (PMID 42298988). The chronic-kidney-disease proposition rests on the edema-stratified kidney-failure progression in the multicenter cohort (PMID 40043694).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) composite-endpoint discipline - the venous anchors measure composite VTE without component separation, so the deep-vein-thrombosis and pulmonary-embolism edges carry the not-separable limit and the arterial endpoints (stroke 8.1 percent, myocardial infarction 6.0 percent at 10 years) are composite components rather than separately powered outcomes; (ii) mechanism honesty - the antithrombin meta-analysis found antithrombin deficiency not a uniform feature and only quantitatively related to hypercoagulability in adults, so the acquired-antithrombin-loss route is carried as limited; (iii) mechanism mix on the myocardial-infarction edge - dyslipidemia mediates part of the coronary risk through atherosclerosis rather than pure thrombosis, recorded on the edge; (iv) histology heterogeneity on the renal edge - minimal change disease remits while membranous and focal-segmental disease progress; (v) prophylaxis-era - albumin-threshold anticoagulation and statin therapy change the event rates captured by these cohorts; (vi) direction discipline - bleeding (adjusted hazard 4.02) is a cohort outcome recorded as a withheld proposition, not an edge.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: First-time nephrotic syndrome documents venous thromboembolism at national matched-cohort and multicenter level: the Danish matched population cohort of 3,967 adults with first-time nephrotic syndrome found 1-year venous thromboembolism risk 2.8 percent and 10-year risk 7.7 percent with first-year adjusted hazard 7.11 versus matched general-population comparators (PMID 34979093), and the Danish multicenter cohort of 1,219 patients with nephrotic-range albuminuria found VTE incidence 15 versus 10 per 1,000 person-years with versus without edema (PMID 40043694), with the multi-cohort study and meta-analysis documenting nephrotic hypercoagulopathy in which antithrombin deficiency plays only a limited role (PMID 36754010); recorded as documented association only, with the composite-VTE endpoint limit carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the anchor cohorts measure composite venous thromboembolism without separating deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and renal vein thrombosis components, so whether any individual deep vein thrombosis is attributable to the nephrotic state requires individual hematology attribution with stasis, malignancy, and thrombophilia exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Urinary loss of natural anticoagulants alongside increased procoagulant factors and platelet activation drives an acquired hypercoagulable state so venous thrombosis results, the procoagulant route documented by the multi-cohort hypercoagulability analysis that found antithrombin deficiency inconsistent and only a limited mechanistic contributor, but whether this route produced any individual thrombosis remains hypothesized until coagulation and imaging records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at national matched cohort plus multicenter cohort class only: both Danish cohorts measure composite VTE endpoints without component separation, the mechanistic meta-analysis found antithrombin deficiency not a uniform feature and quantitatively related to hypercoagulability only in adults, and albumin-threshold-guided anticoagulation prophylaxis changes event rates under contemporary care.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Component-specific deep vein thrombosis rates are not separable from the composite VTE endpoints in either anchor cohort; renal vein thrombosis is classically part of the nephrotic thromboembolism spectrum but unquantified here; the mechanistic meta-analysis found antithrombin deficiency not uniform; and edema-related stasis, immobility, malignancy-associated thrombosis, and inherited thrombophilia overlap the differential.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: malignancy-associated thrombosis (the published cancer thrombosis windows)
immobility and post-surgical venous stasis
inherited thrombophilias
estrogen- and pregnancy-related thrombosis
renal vein thrombosis as a distinct nephrotic complication not in this identity's scope

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Nephrotic-range proteinuric kidney disease documents kidney failure progression at multicenter cohort level: the Danish multicenter cohort of 1,219 patients with nephrotic-range albuminuria and hypoalbuminemia found edema associated with faster kidney failure progression (188 days to kidney failure in edematous versus 364 days in non-edematous patients) alongside higher urine albumin-creatinine ratios and lower plasma albumin (PMID 40043694); recorded as documented association only, scoped to nephrotic-range proteinuric populations with histology-dependent progression carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: nephrotic syndrome spans histologies with very different renal trajectories (minimal change disease responding to immunosuppression versus membranous and focal-segmental disease progressing), so whether any individual chronic kidney disease is attributable to the nephrotic state requires individual nephrology attribution with biopsy histology, treatment-response, and diabetic and obstructive exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Sustained nephrotic-range proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia drives tubular protein toxicity, glomerular hyperfiltration injury, and interstitial fibrosis so chronic kidney disease results, the progression route consistent with the edema-stratified kidney-failure acceleration and the proteinuria-severity gradient in the multicenter cohort, but whether this route produced any individual chronic kidney disease remains hypothesized until biopsy and renal-function records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at single multicenter cohort class only: the anchor measures time-to-kidney-failure stratified by edema rather than etiology-specific progression, histology mix determines trajectory and was recorded but not stratified against the outcome in the located report, and modern immunosuppression and renin-angiotensin blockade alter nephrotic-disease progression.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The anchor cohort reports kidney-failure progression stratified by edema status rather than by histology; minimal change disease often remits with therapy while membranous and focal-segmental disease progress, so the umbrella's trajectory is heterogeneous; no located cohort separates nephrotic-proteinuria-driven progression from underlying histology; and diabetic nephropathy, hypertensive nephrosclerosis, and obstructive uropathy compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: minimal change disease with treatment response and remission
membranous and focal-segmental histology-driven progression (heterogeneity within the umbrella)
diabetic nephropathy (the published diabetic-nephropathy window, not recycled per ME-29)
hypertensive nephrosclerosis (the published hypertension window)
obstructive uropathy and nephrolithiasis sequelae

evidenceGaps: The anchor cohort reports kidney-failure progression stratified by edema status rather than by histology; minimal change disease often remits with therapy while membranous and focal-segmental disease progress, so the umbrella's trajectory is heterogeneous; no located cohort separates nephrotic-proteinuria-driven progression from underlying histology; and diabetic nephropathy, hypertensive nephrosclerosis, and obstructive uropathy compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at multicenter cohort class with the histology-heterogeneity limit carried openly: the Danish multicenter cohort of 1,219 nephrotic-range patients found edema associated with faster kidney failure progression (188 versus 364 days) with proteinuria-severity and hypoalbuminemia gradients (PMID 40043694); because the anchor stratifies by edema rather than histology and nephrotic umbrella trajectories range from treatment-responsive remission to progressive fibrosis, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated renal-function and biopsy review with diabetic, hypertensive, and obstructive exclusion. Sibling separation recorded: this edge rests on nephrotic-range cohort evidence and does not recycle the nephritis window's glomerular-disease cohort anchors (ME-29).
